headline: BNP nominates Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as presidential candidate
summary: The BNP Secretary General has resigned from his party posts to contest the presidency.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has officially nominated Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as its candidate for the presidency of Bangladesh.
Following the nomination, Mirza Fakhrul has resigned from his position as the Secretary General of the BNP and his membership in the party's standing committee.
The party's leadership described Fakhrul as a 'tested' leader, emphasizing his experience and suitability for the highest office in the land.
Mirza Fakhrul has already submitted his nomination papers for the presidential election.
The move marks a significant shift in the party's internal structure as they prepare for the national election process.
Political analysts are now looking at potential successors for the roles Fakhrul previously held within the BNP.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is the BNP's choice for President. He has resigned from all party posts to make the bid.

The party's leadership described Fakhrul as a 'tested' leader, emphasizing his experience and suitability for the highest office in the land.

Mirza Fakhrul has already submitted his nomination papers for the presidential election.

The move marks a significant shift in the party's internal structure as they prepare for the national election process.

Political analysts are now looking at potential successors for the roles Fakhrul previously held within the BNP.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul: [[Bangladesh bowls Australia out for 198]] in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul: Bangladesh bowls Australia out for 198 in Darwin
summary: In a stunning opening day, Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6 for 55 steers the Tigers to a commanding position in the first Test.
details: Bangladesh seized control of the first Test in Darwin, bowling Australia out for 198 in 53 overs on the opening day. The performance was hailed as one of the Tigers' finest days in Test cricket by former Australian leg-spinner Kerry O'Keeffe.
Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, taking 6 wickets for 55 runs. He became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take five wickets in an innings against Australia in Australia.
The Bangladesh seam trio of Hasan, Ebadot Hossain, and Taskin Ahmed utilized the grass on the surface to maintain relentless accuracy, preventing Australian batters from settling.
Steve Smith provided the main resistance for the hosts with 71 runs, but Australia lost wickets regularly throughout the innings.
Bangladesh's batters backed up the bowling effort, reaching 96 for one at stumps. Tanzid Hasan and Mominul Haque remained unbeaten with 32* and 35* respectively.
The Tigers now trail by 102 runs with nine wickets in hand, leaving them in an excellent position to build a substantial first-innings lead on Friday.
caption:
A historic day for the Tigers! Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul destroys Australia for 198.

Bangladesh seized control of the first Test in Darwin, bowling Australia out for 198 in 53 overs on the opening day. The performance was hailed as one of the Tigers' finest days in Test cricket by former Australian leg-spinner Kerry O'Keeffe.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best performance, taking 6 wickets for 55 runs. He became the first Bangladeshi bowler to take five wickets in an innings against Australia in Australia.

The Bangladesh seam trio of Hasan, Ebadot Hossain, and Taskin Ahmed utilized the grass on the surface to maintain relentless accuracy, preventing Australian batters from settling.

Steve Smith provided the main resistance for the hosts with 71 runs, but Australia lost wickets regularly throughout the innings.

Bangladesh's batters backed up the bowling effort, reaching 96 for one at stumps. Tanzid Hasan and Mominul Haque remained unbeaten with 32* and 35* respectively.

The Tigers now trail by 102 runs with nine wickets in hand, leaving them in an excellent position to build a substantial first-innings lead on Friday.
